segments.t: Meanwhile, away from the agency, someone is hiding over lunch. Cécile de France came to the office asking if she still had an agent, because Gabriel never calls her back. Gabriel can't face telling her that Tarantino doesn't want her, so he slipped out to lunch with Sofia, the receptionist. Back at the agency, Camille has just had a row with Mathias, and Noémie has warned her that he is very married. Sofia, though, sees this lunch as her big chance: she is not really a receptionist, she wants to act. Here it is in French first; you don't need every word.
Donc, en fait, je ne suis pas vraiment réceptionniste.
C'est juste un travail pour faire plaisir à ma famille.
À mon banquier aussi.
Parce qu'en fait, je suis comédienne.
Ce vin est incroyablement bon!
Vous l'avez goûté?
Non.
Il est magnifique.
Je joue en ce moment dans un spectacle à la Porte des Lilas.
Porte des Lilas, d'accord.
Ce serait super si vous pouviez venir.
Voilà le flyer. Ça s'appelle Absence.
Merci.
Vous n'êtes pas intéressé?
Non, ce n'est pas ça.
J'ai un problème au boulot.
Un problème au boulot, Gabriel?
Let's go back through it. Sofia takes a deep breath and starts with a confession about her day job.
Donc, en fait, je ne suis pas vraiment réceptionniste.

'So, actually, I'm not really a receptionist.' The two little words at the start are how the French say 'so, in fact', and Sofia leans on them twice in this scene. Notice there's no word for 'a' before a job: you simply say 'I am receptionist'.
C'est juste un travail pour faire plaisir à ma famille.
'It's just a job to make my family happy.' Literally 'to do pleasure to my family'. Then she adds, with a smile...
À mon banquier aussi.
'My banker too.' Because a job pays the rent, after all.
Parce qu'en fait, je suis comédienne.
'Because actually, I'm an actress.' That's the word for a stage and screen actress. Again, no word for 'an' before it. And Gabriel? He's busy with his glass.
Ce vin est incroyablement bon!
'This wine is incredibly good!' Gabriel combines 'this' with 'good' in a natural French turn of phrase.
Vous l'avez goûté?
'Have you tasted it?' The small word before the verb stands for 'it', the wine. He's polite: the formal 'you'.
Non.
'No.' She hasn't touched it; she's too busy pitching.
Il est magnifique.
'It's magnificent.' He's talking about the wine, of course, not about her play. Sofia tries again.
Je joue en ce moment dans un spectacle à la Porte des Lilas.
'I'm in a show at the moment, at the Porte des Lilas.' The verb means 'to play', and it's also how you say 'to act'. The Porte des Lilas is a district on the edge of Paris.
Porte des Lilas, d'accord.
'Porte des Lilas, right.' He just repeats the name, the way you do when you're not really listening.
Ce serait super si vous pouviez venir.
'It would be great if you could come.' A very polite way to invite someone. Learn it as one block: 'it would be great', then 'if you could come'.
Voilà le flyer.
'Here's the flyer.' This handy word means 'here it is', when you hand something over. The French borrow the English word for the leaflet.
Ça s'appelle Absence.
'It's called Absence.' Literally 'it calls itself Absence', the same pattern French uses to say your own name.
Merci.
'Thank you.' And then a long silence.
Vous n'êtes pas intéressé?
'You're not interested?' A question made just by raising the voice at the end. The negative wraps around the verb: a small word before, the word for 'not' after.
Non, ce n'est pas ça.
'No, it's not that.' He means: it's not you. Then he admits what's really on his mind.
J'ai un problème au boulot.
'I've got a problem at work.' The word for 'work' here is the casual, everyday one; you'll hear it all the time.
Un problème au boulot, Gabriel?
'A problem at work, Gabriel?' And that voice belongs to Cécile, who has found him. The problem has just walked up to his table. Here's the whole lunch again, in French.
Donc, en fait, je ne suis pas vraiment réceptionniste.
C'est juste un travail pour faire plaisir à ma famille.
À mon banquier aussi.
Parce qu'en fait, je suis comédienne.
Ce vin est incroyablement bon!
Vous l'avez goûté?
Non.
Il est magnifique.
Je joue en ce moment dans un spectacle à la Porte des Lilas.
Porte des Lilas, d'accord.
Ce serait super si vous pouviez venir.
Voilà le flyer. Ça s'appelle Absence.
Merci.
Vous n'êtes pas intéressé?
Non, ce n'est pas ça.
J'ai un problème au boulot.
Un problème au boulot, Gabriel?
Well done: you just sat through Sofia's first pitch in French. Listen for 'I'm an actress' when you watch, and for the moment Cécile walks in. Until next time.
Au revoir!
